- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment shift > +0.2.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early 30-day horizon — overcorrects downward after recent highs; apply 1–2% upward bias if prior 7-day avg > 70.0.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment > +0.2 for 3+ consecutive days, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often underestimates true volatility; increase forecast by 0.3–0.7% if sentiment < -0.1 and price > 70.0.
